transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (Aurora Head of ML), Tom Reyes (CTO), Leila Brooks (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood and Aurora scoped a short POC to evaluate open-source models for clinical note summarization and triage. Focus: model shortlist, dataset samples (multi-lingual), benchmarks (latency, p95, throughput), quality metrics (ROUGE/BERTscore/custom medical entity F1), and timeline ~3-4 weeks. Discussed tradeoffs between larger models and quantization, Dedicated vs Hosted for latency-sensitive paths, and compliance controls (SOC2, VPC, KMS). Next steps and owners captured.

Topics: model shortlist, sample dataset, benchmark plan, success criteria, infra choice, timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to kick off with what success looks like for you for this POC, Dana, do you want to lead?
[00:08] Dana Liu: Yeah thanks, hi. So main thing is accuracy on clinical summarization, and extraction of key med entities. Also latency matters for our triage flow — we need sub-700ms p95 in the fastest path, but ok with more for batch. We also need Spanish and Portuguese coverage, so multilingual is required.
[00:28] Tom Reyes: And from infra side we need to understand data residency and encryption, we'll probably run initial experiments with hosted but Dedicated if latency can't meet our SLOs. Also SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves.
[00:40] Marco Ruiz: Got it. Quick clarifying q — when you say sub-700ms p95, is that for the whole request including network, or just inference?
[00:47] Leila Brooks: For the product we measure end-to-end, but for the POC we can slice it — inference-only p95 target around 450-500ms would be great.
[00:55] Sofia Patel: That helps. Ok so model shortlist — we've suggested a few open candidates based on prior med-domain work and multilingual capabilities: Llama 3 13B (quantized), Mistral Large 7B variant, Falcon-40B-instruct, and Mixtral / Mixtra-lite (OpenAssistant derivatives). Marco, can you walk through perf expectations and quantization tradeoffs?
[01:15] Marco Ruiz: Yeah. So rough ballpark — on a single A100-style GPU: Llama3-13B 4-bit quantized can hit around 300-450ms per request at 512 tokens when optimized, p95 depends on batching; Mistral-7B is faster and cheaper but may lag on clinical nuance; Falcon-40B is higher quality on some clinical prompts but costlier and needs more memory, might need Dedicated or SPMD for throughput. Mixtral variants are interesting, good middle ground. Also we can try q4f16 / nf4 quant to reduce memory footprint. Note: transcription may call it "Redword" sometimes, ignore that — lol.
[01:55] Dana Liu: Mm-hmm. How are you measuring quality, like what metrics will you run?
[02:00] Marco Ruiz: We'll run automatic metrics: ROUGE, BERTScore, medical entity F1 using your gold extracts if provided. We'll also add a small human-blind eval on 100 samples for clinical acceptability. For multilingual we'll run per-language slices.
[02:18] Leila Brooks: For our business criteria, if entity F1 dips below 0.82 on English we consider it fail, and acceptable for Spanish/Portuguese is 0.78. Also we need hallucination checks for meds — precision is very important.
[02:30] Sofia Patel: Noted. Timeline question: how long to get initial bench results? Marco?
[02:33] Marco Ruiz: If we get the 1k samples by Friday, we can run a 1k-sample benchmark across the shortlist within 4 business days, share an annotated spreadsheet with p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-request, cost-per-token estimate, and the quality metrics I mentioned. So that lands around next Monday/Tuesday.
[02:50] Tom Reyes: OK. About infrastructure — if we do Hosted vs Dedicated, what's the gating?
[02:55] Sofia Patel: Hosted is fastest to ship and we can do the benchmark there; Dedicated is recommended if p95 inference or throughput can't meet your SLOs on hosted hardware or if you need strict tenancy/residency. We can also do a hybrid: routing latency-sensitive traffic to Dedicated and background batch on Hosted.
[03:13] Dana Liu: For encryption, we need KMS + HSM option and audit logs retained 1 year. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[03:20] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Private/Dedicated supports customer KMS integration and audit logs. Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and a managed KMS, but if you need CMK we recommend Dedicated/Private deployment.
[03:30] Leila Brooks: Any red flags on licensing for these open models? Some of our legal folks worry about Llama licensing.
[03:36] Sofia Patel: Good point — we will surface license notes in the model sheet. Llama 3 family may have usage terms; Mistral and Falcon variants vary, we'll flag anything that requires restrictions and proposed mitigations.
[03:46] Marco Ruiz: Also, for quantization we sometimes see quality degradation on entity-level recall — so we'll capture per-model calibration curves.
[03:54] Dana Liu: For multilingual, do you recommend fine-tuning or instruction-tuning? We don't have labeled train data beyond those 1k samples.
[04:01] Marco Ruiz: For 1k, we wouldn't recommend full fine-tune. We'll use prompt engineering plus small few-shot examples and parameter-efficient tuning (LoRA) only if we hit a quality ceiling and have at least a few hundred labeled examples per language.
[04:14] Leila Brooks: Is there a way to quickly test hallucination on meds?
[04:17] Marco Ruiz: We'll run targeted factuality tests — masked entity recovery and med-term precision tests. Also set up a post-hoc verifier if needed.
[04:24] Tom Reyes: About cost — can you give a sense of per-request cost differential?
[04:28] Sofia Patel: Ballpark: Mistral-7B quantized is lowest cost per token, Llama3-13B 4-bit is middle, Falcon-40B highest. Our benchmark spreadsheet will include estimated cost-per-inference using your average tokens/request. We'll model a 100k-month volume to show ROI.
[04:45] Dana Liu: For success criteria recap — accuracy thresholds, p95 inference targets, and operational gating like KMS and logs. Anything else?
[04:52] Sofia Patel: Also regression on hallucination for meds and a pass on multilingual thresholds. We'll capture formal success criteria in the POC charter.
[04:59] Marco Ruiz: Practical note — can you confirm the avg tokens/request? Earlier you mentioned ~320 tokens for summary generation and 90 for extractive tasks.
[05:05] Dana Liu: Yes, that's accurate: 320 tokens typical for summary, 80-120 for extraction. We'll include edge cases up to 1,200 tokens but those are batch jobs.
[05:13] Leila Brooks: Ok. For the benchmark, please include p50/p95/p99 and cost per request, and separate columns for per-language performance.
[05:20] Marco Ruiz: Will do. Also noting we may try a hybrid quantization approach — q4 and q8 mix, and pruning in the evaluation.
[05:29] Tom Reyes: Any concerns about tokenization differences between models?
[05:32] Marco Ruiz: Yep tokenizers differ, we'll normalize metrics to tokens-per-request as processed by each model and also report character-level metrics for fairness.
[05:40] Sofia Patel: Great. Next steps recap: Dana will share 1k-sample, Sofia to send SOW/pricing, Marco to run benchmarks and share spreadsheet, then follow-up deep-dive on infra.
[05:54] Dana Liu: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:57] Sofia Patel: Thank you — we'll aim to have the first pass by next Tuesday.
[06:00] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains typical ASR errors (names/brand words), timestamps approximate. References to model names may be slightly off in the audio; refer to the model sheet that Redwood will attach for exact tags.
